title: prefill-granularity-adaptation-and-decode-slip-controller
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Improve latency tail and throughput stability by dynamically resizing prefill chunk granularity and adding a decode-slip controller to avoid decode stalls. No API changes.
description: Context: Large variance in sequence-length mixes causes the static-chunking heuristic to either over-prefill (high tail latency) or under-utilize kernels (reduced throughput). This PR introduces two coordinated mechanisms: 1) a prefill granularity adapter that tunes chunk sizes per-worker based on online sequence-length statistics with hysteresis to avoid oscillation; 2) a decode-slip controller that detects and corrects 'decode slips' where decode work lags prefill progress, by selectively throttling new prefill chunks and prioritizing KV preheat for imminent decodes. Motivation: reduce p95/p99 tail latencies without sacrificing average throughput across mixed workloads. Summary of changes: - runtime/scheduler: add prefill_resizer module that maintains an EWMA of token lengths and chooses chunk targets; includes hysteresis thresholds and a bounded resize rate to keep stability; implements a small state machine to yield or coalesce chunk requests when downstream decode queue depth is high - runtime/scheduler: introduce decode_slip_controller that observes per-stream decode lag (tokens in prefill minus tokens decoded) and issues backpressure signals to the prefill allocator; exposes metrics for slip_score and corrective_actions - runtime/kernel: lightweight hint API to mark KV ranges for prioritized preheat so urgent decodes get hot KV - runtime/kvcache: add prioritized_get path used by decode_slip_controller to prefetch small warmups - perf tests and benchmarks: perf/prefill_adapt_bench.py and benchmark matrices in .github/workflows/perf-matrix.yml - docs: docs/architecture/prefill-adapt.md with operator knobs and recommended defaults Compatibility: behavior defaults conservatively to existing static chunking when feature gate is off. Rollout plan: start with Canary-1 region, enable on a 10% share for 48h, evaluate slip_score and p99 latency regressions. Checklist: - Design doc reviewed and linked (ENG-1948); - Unit tests for state machine and controller added; - Perf harness added and runs in CI; - Docs updated with operator guidance; - Feature gated and runtime flag controlled; - No public API changes; See also related PRs for scheduling heuristics and KV prefetching.

review_comments: Liam O'Connor (2026-02-20): Can you add a short experiment showing stability over a 24h trace? The EWMA time-constant feels like it could chase diurnal patterns.
Priya Nair (2026-02-21): Added a config knob and bounded resize rate; uploaded a 24h trace run to the perf artifact and linked in the design doc.
Miguel Torres (2026-02-23): Risk: prioritized_get path could add contention on hot KV shards. Suggested adding a small token bucket on prioritized requests. Added in latest commit.
Ava Chen (2026-02-25): Unit tests look good, but please add an assertion that hysteresis prevents immediate up/down toggles when fed micro-bursts.
Liam O'Connor (2026-03-01): Verified perf artifacts; p95 down 18% and p99 down 27% on mixed-seq benchmark in Canary sim. Approving.
Release/Infra Bot (2026-03-01): perf-matrix workflow completed: 1 flaky perf test re-run; final status PASS.
benchmark_results: mixed-seq workload (64/128/512 mix): baseline p95=68ms p99=204ms; this PR p95=56ms p99=149ms
throughput: steady-state token/s within 3% of baseline for high-concurrency runs; improvement on mixed small/large batch scenarios due to reduced KV stall smoothing
cpu/gpu timelines: fewer long-tail stalls recorded; average KV preheat ops up 6% but with 22% fewer decode retries
notes_for_ops: Feature is behind runtime flag: --enable-prefill-adapt (default false in canary)
Operator knobs documented: ewma_window_ms, hysteresis_pct, max_resize_per_min, slip_threshold
Recommended rollout: 10% traffic Canary for 48h, verify slip_score < 0.05 and p99 improvement >= 10% before wider rollout
